entry.title: Exploring the Tractability Frontier of Hylland-Zeckhauser Models
entry.summary:
The Hylland-Zeckhauser (HZ) mechanism provides a market-based approach to one-sided matching, making efficient equilibrium computation central to its implementation. Bi-valued utilities admit a strongly polynomial-time algorithm [VY], whereas with four values per buyer, the problem is PPAD-hard under inverse polynomial approximation [CCPY]. To understand the tractability boundary, we study two extensions of the bi-valued case: a third linear utility value and separable concave utilities with two common marginal slopes.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Information-thermodynamic principles unveil the response of complex networks to perturbations
entry.summary:
Understanding how complex networks respond to perturbations is key to uncovering their functional organization. We show that, for a maximum-entropy perturbation prior, standard diffusion cannot increase response entropy, a measure of the diversity of the system's response. To overcome this limitation, we develop a density-matrix-based information thermodynamics of perturbation responses along arbitrary dynamical trajectories.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #clean-tech #computer-vision

entry.title: Formation of international environmental agreements and payoff allocation. Dealing with climate change requires that all countries engage in costly efforts to reduce their emissions.
entry.summary:
Dealing with climate change requires that all countries engage in costly efforts to reduce their emissions. Reaching this objective has so far been elusive because it is in the best interest of each country to let the others do the effort and benefit itself from a better environment. The presence of negative externalities and strategic behavior have made game theory a natural paradigm to design an international environmental agreement (IEA) that codifies what countries should do.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Assortment Optimization and Matching under MNL Choice
entry.summary:
We develop a unified framework for assortment optimization and matching under multinomial logit (MNL) choice, yielding simple algorithms and analyses across a broad class of problems. The framework centers on a single-customer assortment problem in which the firm commits to eligible products before their independent availabilities are revealed. A simple threshold policy achieves a tight $1/2$ guarantee against a benchmark that selects its assortment after observing availability and may control dependence subject to the same marginal probability bounds.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #optimization

entry.title: Who Pays for Thinking? Billing Hidden Reasoning Tokens in Model Cloud Contracts
entry.summary:
In token-priced language model services, users can see the prompts they submit and the answers they receive, but may also pay for internal reasoning and candidate answers that are not shown in the final response. This paper develops a three-party service model to study how charging for this intermediate computation shapes providers' decisions and social welfare. Users purchase answers from a model firm that pays an execution cloud, with either supplier controlling the computation budget.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: BROCADE: Broker-based Contract Design for the Multi-Agency Model
entry.summary:
We study welfare maximization in a contract model with $m$ principals who privately value a public project's success and $n$ agents whose costly effort is unobservable. Contracts induce truthful dominant strategies for principals and equilibrium effort by agents, maximizing the expected total value of eligible principals. We develop three tools: a broker that separates payments from principals and payments to agents, an extension of Myerson's Lemma characterizing dominant-strategy incentive compatibility (DSIC), and a black-box reduction to budget-constrained single-principal contract design.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents

entry.title: Multiplex relational event models of self-reported and perceived gossip. Gossiping is a complex social phenomenon that unfolds through multiple types of relations.
entry.summary:
Gossiping is a complex social phenomenon that unfolds through multiple types of relations. Among other things, individuals may initiate gossiping about others as a result of believing themselves to be the target of gossip. These two processes, i.e., gossiping and gossip perception, form a dynamic multiplex network, where self-reported and perceived gossip ties coexist and can influence each other over time.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Follow the Regularized Leader Does Not Converge in Constrained Optimization
entry.summary:
Follow the regularized leader (FTRL) is a foundational algorithm in online learning whose regret properties have been extensively studied for decades. However, in stark contrast to mirror descent---and gradient descent in particular---the convergence of FTRL to first-order stationary points in constrained nonconvex optimization was not well understood. In this paper, we show that continuous-time FTRL can fail to converge even asymptotically in infinitely smooth constrained optimization problems: its Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) gap can remain bounded away from zero indefinitely.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #optimization

entry.title: Fair Division of Lotteries
entry.summary:
We study fair division of uncertain items, where the utility of each item is a random variable whose realization is observed only after the allocation is determined. This uncertainty creates a distinction between ex-ante fairness, evaluated before utilities are realized, and ex-post fairness, evaluated after realization. We examine to what extent these two notions are compatible.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #agents
